title: How Much Fiber in Navy Beans? 19.1g per Cup
description: Navy Beans: about 19.1 g of fiber per 1 cup, cooked (68% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in navy beans?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Beans, navy, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt

intro: Navy beans rank #1 of 10 beans and legumes on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in navy beans by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in navy beans?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists beans, navy, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt at 10.5 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup, cooked; 182 g) therefore has about 19.1 g of fiber and 255 calories. That is 68% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 76% of a 25 g day and 50% of a 38 g day.
Navy beans are small white beans used in baked beans and white bean soups. Per cooked cup, they carry the most fiber of any bean on this site, more than black, pinto, or kidney beans.

sections.heading: Navy beans vs canned baked beans
paragraphs: Baked beans are usually made from navy beans, but the canned product includes a sweet tomato sauce. The beans still bring fiber, yet a cup of baked beans contains fewer beans and more sugar than a cup of plain cooked navy beans. Use the can’s label for baked beans.
Plain navy beans have a mild, creamy texture that disappears into soups and purées, which makes them an easy way to add fiber to a dish without changing its flavor much.

sections.heading: How navy beans compare with other beans and legumes
paragraphs: Of the 10 beans and legumes on this site, navy beans rank #1 for fiber per typical serving and #1 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 7.5 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [split peas](/fiber-in-split-peas) at 16.3 g (1 cup, cooked); [lentils](/fiber-in-lentils) at 15.6 g (1 cup, cooked); [pinto beans](/fiber-in-pinto-beans) at 15.4 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), navy beans are #11 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding navy beans to your day
paragraphs: Blend half a cup into a pasta sauce or soup for creaminess, or toss with olive oil, lemon, and herbs as a side. Because the fiber is so concentrated, increase portions gradually.

Example: 1/2 cup navy beans, 2 slices whole wheat bread, 1 cup spinach. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 14.1 g of fiber, with 9.6 g from the navy beans. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of navy beans?
faqs.a: 10.5 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Beans, navy, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in navy beans (1/2 cup, cooked)?
faqs.a: About 9.6 g, for 91 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: Are navy beans and cannellini beans the same?
faqs.a: No. Both are white beans, but cannellini beans are larger and kidney-shaped. Their fiber is in a similar range; navy bean figures on this page come from USDA’s navy bean entry.

faqs.q: Is one cup of navy beans too much fiber at once?
faqs.a: For someone used to beans, many people tolerate it fine. If your usual intake is low, start with a quarter or half cup and drink water with it, then build up over a few weeks.
